The Food Bridge
Every Campus Needs

Anna-Setu (अन्न सेतु) - Hindi for "Food Bridge"

Every day, campus dining halls cook 20-40% more food than students eat, sending it to landfill while millions go hungry. Anna-Setu checks food safety in seconds, matches surplus to the nearest shelter, and turns plate waste into soil conditioner - zero to landfill.

The Problem

India's food loss problem starts in institutional kitchens -
campuses are a silent contributor.

Institutional kitchens over-produce by 20-40% using fixed static buffers (source needed - adjust with your campus data). Food that could nourish people instead becomes methane-emitting landfill or municipal waste. FSSAI Surplus Food Regulations 2019 require safe redistribution, but none of the campus-ready digital tools we could find implement them end-to-end.

19 Cr
People undernourished in India (FAO 2023)
~40%
Food lost or wasted post-harvest in India (est. - verify with FSSAI/ICAR)
8-10%

2019
FSSAI Surplus Food Regulations - no campus tool we could find implements them
How it Works

Two Tracks. Six Steps.

Anna-Setu runs two parallel tracks - Track A (digital safety & rescue) and Track B (physical plate-waste recycler).

Track A - Surplus Food Rescue

📋
A1

Log the Surplus

Kitchen staff enter food item, cooking time and storage condition. Takes under 60 seconds.

🛡️
A2

Rule-Based Safety Check

Deterministic rules grounded in FSSAI Surplus Food Regulations 2019 return a 🟢 / 🟡 / 🔴 verdict. Rules decide safety - not an LLM.

🏠
A3

Match & Alert Shelter

The nearest sample Rain Basera shelter is matched by zone. A WhatsApp-ready advance notice is generated instantly.

Track B - Plate-Waste Recycler

♻️
B1

Weigh Plate Scraps

Track B concept: an IoT kiosk at the tray-return counter weighs plate scraps and nudges diners with their water and carbon footprint.

🌱
B2

PTC Bio-Recycler

PTC ceramic heating + aerobic aeration converts food scraps into dry pre-compost biomass within 24 hours - pending NPK testing for use as soil conditioner.

📊
B3

Demand Estimator

Attendance multipliers for day, weather and academic calendar help kitchens cook closer to actual demand - reducing surplus before it starts.

Platform Features

Everything in One Place

Available on Streamlit - designed for dining hall staff, wardens, and sustainability officers.

⚖️

Deterministic Safety Rules

Safety verdicts come from FSSAI Surplus Food Regulations 2019 category time limits - deterministic rules, not an LLM. Every result cites the governing clause.

🔍

Keyword-Based Clause Retriever

The Q&A module retrieves relevant FSSAI and LNN clauses by keyword matching and assembles a plain-English explanation. IBM Granite integration is on the roadmap.

📍

Zone-Based Shelter Matching

6+ sample Lucknow Rain Basera shelters indexed by zone and capacity. Confirm shelter FSSAI registration and live availability before dispatch.

📱

WhatsApp Advance Notice

One-tap copy of a donation advance notice with food details, pickup location and timing. Logged against Schedule II fields for FSSAI compliance.

🔮

Demand Estimator

Attendance multipliers for day-of-week, weather and exam schedule help set cooking targets. Modelled estimate - actual savings depend on kitchen baseline.

💬

Plain-English Q&A

Ask "Can I donate rice after 3 hours?" and get a clause-backed answer from the embedded rule base - accessible to all staff levels.

Modelled Impact

The Numbers That Matter

Modelled estimates - 850-diner hall, 240 operating days/year, 10% plate-waste kiosk capture assumption. All figures are projections, not measured outcomes. GHG factor ~1.9 kg CO₂e/kg is unverified against IPCC AR5 Tier 1 exactly - treat as approximate.

12,000+
Meals potentially rescued per year (Track A, 20% of surplus, 0.35 kg/meal, modelled)
~4.2 MT
Surplus food redirected from landfill (Track A, 12,000 meals × 0.35 kg)
~535 kg
Dry pre-compost biomass per year (Track B, 850 diners × 10% capture × 15% yield × 240 days, pending NPK testing)
~8 MT
CO₂e avoided approx (Track A rescued food × ~1.9 kg CO₂e/kg - factor unverified, treat as estimate)
₹8.4L
Kitchen procurement savings (modelled, 20% overproduction reduction)
~3,200 KL
Embedded freshwater preserved (Track A: 4.2 MT × 760 L/kg, Mekonnen & Hoekstra 2011)
UN Sustainable Development Goals

Built for the Goals That Matter Most

Anna-Setu directly targets 4 United Nations SDGs with specific, verifiable contributions. Each is linked to a primary target indicator.

12
Responsible Consumption
Target 12.3 - halve per capita food waste. Demand estimation reduces overproduction.
2
Zero Hunger
Target 2.1 - safe, nutritious food access. Surplus meals redirected to Rain Basera shelters.
13
Climate Action
Target 13.2 - reduce methane from landfill food waste. Modelled GHG avoidance cited with IPCC factor.
11
Sustainable Cities
Target 11.6 - reduce municipal waste. On-site bio-recycler diverts organic waste from city landfill.
